candidate.answerReason: A listed total requires zero pennies, so four coins have value at least 20 cents. Each other listed total has a four-coin construction.

methods.label: Restrict the pennies, then use a minimum
methods.explanation:
The coin values are \(1,5,10,25\) cents. Every listed total is a multiple of \(5\), and every coin other than a penny also has a value that is a multiple of \(5\).

Let \(p\) be the number of pennies among the four coins. Subtracting the value of the other coins from a listed total shows that \(p\) must be a multiple of \(5\). Since \(0\le p\le4\), we must have \(p=0\). Thus all four coins are worth at least \(5\) cents each, making their total at least \(20\) cents. A total of \(15\) cents is impossible.

Each remaining total can be made with exactly four coins:
\[
\begin{aligned}
25&=5+5+5+10,\\
35&=5+10+10+10,\\
45&=25+10+5+5,\\
55&=25+10+10+10.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore the only impossible listed total is \(15\) cents, choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
